tasks.task: Establish site, mobilise scaffold, brief occupants
tasks.scope: Set up site office, mobilise scaffold components via Kiora Lane and courtyard, erect temporary hoarding, conduct occupant induction and exclusion briefing, confirm Leo and Associates contact and inspection scheduling
hazards: Trip hazard from scaffold components and mobile equipment on Kiora Lane and courtyard
Struck-by hazard from moving scaffold delivery vehicle in occupied courtyard
Manual handling injury during scaffold component handling and positioning
Noise exposure from scaffold installation activities affecting occupant amenity
tasks.dominant_hazard: Struck-by hazard from scaffold delivery vehicle
controls: Confirm Leo and Associates contact and inspection schedule before mobilisation begins.
Barricade Kiora Lane access point and courtyard delivery route with tape and signs. Post spotters at entry and exit points.
Brief all site personnel on vehicle approach path, pedestrian exclusion zones, and stop signals before delivery vehicle enters site.
Park scaffold delivery vehicle in courtyard with hazard lights on. Reverse spotters to guide load positioning away from building facade.
Carry or drag scaffold components along marked pathways only. Keep Kiora Lane clear of components between trips.
Stack scaffold components in designated storage area outside occupied building entrance. Secure stacks against movement.
Erect temporary hoarding around scaffold footprint before assembly starts. Verify hoarding is secure and fully enclosed.
Conduct occupant induction briefing before scaffold erection commences. Cover noise times, access restrictions, and emergency procedures.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold until: Leo and Associates contact confirms inspection scheduling is available and Leo and Associates site representative or approved delegate has briefed the licenced scaffolder on building constraints and load limits.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit any worker to use completed scaffold until: licenced scaffolder has issued signed scaffold handover certificate and Leo and Associates has countersigned acceptance.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold delivery vehicle contact with occupied areas occurs or occupants re-enter exclusion zone during mobilisation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: temporary hoarding is incomplete, damaged, or does not fully enclose scaffold footprint.
🛑 STOP WORK if: licenced scaffolder cannot confirm load-bearing capacity or building constraints before assembly begins.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Obtain signed working at heights permit before any elevated task commences.
Provide noise management plan to building management. Schedule noisy activities outside occupant quiet hours if practicable.
Record occupant induction attendance and topics covered. Retain record on site.
Verify all site personnel hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001).
Verify licenced scaffolder holds current scaffolding licence appropriate to scaffold type and height.
Verify all personnel assigned to elevated work hold current working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or current equivalent).
Brief site induction must include: scaffold exclusion zones, Kiora Lane access protocol, occupant contact protocols, and emergency assembly point.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement

Safety helmet — worn during scaffold mobilisation and assembly.
steel-capped footwear— worn during handling and assembly.
Hearing protection (Class A earmuffs or Class C foam plugs) — worn during scaffold assembly if noise exceeds 85 dB(A).

monitoring.who: Licenced scaffolder and Leo and Associates site representative
monitoring.frequency: Once, before scaffold assembly commences
monitoring.evidence: Signed scaffold erection permit and handover certificate; photograph of hoarding perimeter and exclusion zone signage; occupant induction attendance register

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Erect scaffold and edge protection over balconies
tasks.scope: Install scaffold framework, guardrails, and edge protection to all active balconies. Confirm load ratings and stability before work commencement. Exclude occupants from areas directly below active balconies throughout works
hazards: Fall from height during scaffold erection — loss of footing or slip on balcony edge
Collapse or instability of partially erected scaffold framework
Dropped tools or scaffold components from height onto workers or occupants below
Inadequate anchor point failure or guardrail deflection under load
Fall from scaffold platform edge due to gap in edge protection during erection
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — collapse of partially erected scaffold or loss of footing
controls: Obtain and display scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder before any framework assembly starts.
Verify ground and base conditions are level, compacted, and capable of supporting proposed load — document findings before erection commences.
Erect scaffold in sequence strictly following engineer-approved detail plan — do not deviate or omit sections.
Install edge protection (guardrails 1100–1200 mm high, mid-rail, toe boards) on all open sides of scaffold platform and balcony edges during erection, not after.
Secure all horizontal and vertical framework connections with certified fastenings — tighten and check all connections before next level is added.
Install and tag each completed section with handover tag — do not allow work above until tag is affixed and section is load-tested.
Barricade area directly below active balconies and scaffold — restrict occupants and workers not on scaffold from entering exclusion zone.
Check all anchor points are fixed to structural elements capable of sustaining 6 kN load — tag each anchor and record location.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold above ground level until: licenced scaffolder has verified ground condition and baseplate load distribution is correct and documented.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker onto completed scaffold platform until: handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder confirming all connections are tight, guardrails are secure, and load test is passed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any connection is found loose, guardrail is bent or incomplete, or baseplate is shifting or settling.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker enters exclusion zone below active balconies or if occupants are found in direct fall line.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind exceeds 40 km/h or weather conditions make scaffold platform slippery.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Brief all workers on scaffold erection sequence, permitted loading, and exclusion zone rules before work starts.
Obtain working at heights permit signed by site supervisor before each day's elevated tasks start.
Record daily checks in site logbook — include time, inspector name, defects found, and remedial action.
tell building occupants of exclusion zone below active balconies — post warning signage at all entry points.
Obtain noise management plan if scaffold erection generates noise exceeding 75 dB(A) — co-ordinate timing with occupancy.
ppe: Safety harness and lanyard (when on incomplete scaffold or above 2 m)
Eye protection — if cutting or fastening scaffold members

monitoring.critical_control: Check all connections are tight and guardrails are secure before platform use.
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift and after any modification
monitoring.evidence: Handover certificate, daily check logbook, signed inspection tags on each section

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Remove existing membrane, screed, and tile bed
tasks.scope: Strip existing waterproofing membrane, screed layer, and tile bed from balcony surfaces. Manage dust and debris containment. Segregate waste for disposal. Expose slab substrate. Work may produce silica dust — control per Safe Work Australia Code of Practice — Construction Work
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust from cutting and grinding membrane, screed, and tile
Fall from height from active balcony edge during removal work
Hand or foot injury from sharp tile edges and broken tile fragments
Struck-by hazard from flying tile or debris fragments during removal
Musculoskeletal strain from heavy screed and tile removal and manual handling
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust — sustained exposure during demolition
controls: Wet suppress all cutting, grinding, and tile breaking — use water spray or wet-cutting equipment to prevent dust release.
Connect dust extraction to all power tools — grinder, angle cutter, breaker — before starting work each shift.
Wear P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted and checked before work starts; change cartridge if breathing becomes harder or smell detected.
Contain debris within exclusion zone — erect dust barrier or sheeting around active removal area to stop debris spread.
Remove broken tile and screed fragments by damp wiping or wet vacuum — do not dry sweep or blow.
Segregate tile, membrane, and screed waste into separate bins — label hazmat containers if membrane contains asbestos (see latent condition note).
Check scaffold edge protection and handrails before crew access — verify no gaps or damage in guardrails.
Wear cut-resistant gloves and steel-capped boots — change gloves immediately if torn or contaminated.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start removal until: scaffold has been checked, tagged, and handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not expose slab substrate until: completed section has been checked for contamination and confirmed fit for next trade.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression system fails or dust extraction disconnects during active grinding or cutting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any tile, debris, or material falls outside containment zone or exclusion barrier is breached.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unknown material (suspected asbestos, lead, or hazardous contamination) is encountered — do not disturb; report to site supervisor.
admin: Provide SDS for membrane product on point of use — show to all workers before task starts.
Brief all workers on silica hazard, wet suppression method, and dust extraction use before first cut or grind.
Record daily dust suppression checks — confirm water supply, extraction power, and P2 cartridge replacement in site log.
Establish traffic control and signage to prevent occupant access to work area during removal.
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) — fitted and checked each shift; cartridge changed when airflow resistance increases or odour detected.
Steel-capped boots — oil and slip resistant.
Dust coat or disposable coveralls if asbestos suspected (latent condition — see controls).

monitoring.critical_control: Confirm water supply flowing and dust extraction running continuously during all cutting and grinding.
monitoring.who: Site Supervisor — every 30 minutes during active removal; Workers — at task start and after equipment restart.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during removal work; documented shift start and equipment change logs.
monitoring.evidence: Water supply pressure gauge reading on hose; dust extraction power indicator lit; P2 cartridge date and replacement log; daily site log entry confirming suppression status.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove existing membrane, screed, and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing membrane, screed, and per SWMS

tasks.task: Expose and clean slab substrate for inspection
tasks.scope: Remove residual screed and adhesive. Clean slab surface to reveal all cracks, spalling, and surface defects. Prepare substrate ready for Leo and Associates inspection and approval before membrane application
hazards: Inhalation of dust and residual particles during screed and adhesive removal
Cut or laceration from scraper tools and grinding equipment
Fall from height while cleaning edges and perimeter of balcony slab
Musculoskeletal strain from repetitive scraping and cleaning motions
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during edge and perimeter cleaning work
controls: Erect and install fall arrest system (harness anchor point) before any worker accesses slab edge or perimeter. Attach to certified fixed point minimum 1.2 m above working surface.
Wear full-body harness clipped to anchor point always while within 2 m of slab edge. Check harness webbing and attachment points before each shift.
Install edge protection (guardrail or certified edge barrier) minimum 1.1 m height along all slab edges accessible during cleaning. Maintain gap-free coverage.
Wet-suppress all screed and adhesive removal work. Apply water spray during scraping and grinding to control dust generation at source.
Use dust extraction equipment (HEPA-filtered vacuum or extractor) during all dry grinding or scraping tasks. Maintain suction continuously during grinding.
Wear respiratory protective equipment (P2 or P3 mask) during all dust-generating tasks. Change mask when clogged or after 8 hours continuous use.
Use handheld scrapers and grinders with two-hand control and dead-man trigger. Never force or jam tools into substrate.
Wear cut-resistant gloves (Level 4 minimum) when handling scraper tools and broken screed edges. check gloves for tears before each use.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start cleaning work until: scaffolding handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and harness anchor points are inspected and approved by site supervisor
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to membrane application until: Leo and Associates has inspected and signed off on substrate condition, cracks, and spalling defects
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: harness becomes detached from anchor point, anchor point shows visible damage or loosening, or worker moves beyond 2 m safe distance from edge
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression system fails, water supply stops, or dust extraction vacuum loses suction during grinding or scraping
🛑 STOP WORK if: unexpected substrate condition found (asbestos suspect material, extensive spalling, or structural damage) — do not proceed until condition assessed and Leo and Associates advises
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Record all tool inspections, PPE changes, harness checks, and any stop-work incidents in site diary.
Establish emergency contact procedure and rescue plan for fall from height incident. Brief all workers on emergency response location and assembly point.

Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Full-body harness with certified lanyard and clip
P2 or P3 respiratory protective equipment (mask)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during elevated work; minimum 15-minute visual check interval
monitoring.evidence: Supervisor observation log; photographic record of harness engagement and edge barrier integrity; dust suppression water flow visual confirmation

tasks.task: Leo and Associates check slab and approve substrate
tasks.scope: Hold point. Contractor to engage Leo and Associates for full visual inspection of slab cracks, spalling, and substrate condition. Document findings. No membrane application may start until written approval is received and slab repair scope is confirmed
hazards: Fall from height during inspector access and movement across balcony slab
Trip hazard from uneven or damaged slab surface during inspection walkover
Struck-by hazard if worker falls or loses balance during visual inspection
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during slab inspection
controls: Confirm scaffold erection permit signed by licensed scaffolder and handover certificate received before any inspector accesses scaffold.
Verify working at heights permit signed and current before inspection commences.
Confirm Leo and Associates inspector holds current White Card and working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Install edge protection (guardrail minimum 1.0 m height) around all balcony slab perimeter where scaffold platform exceeds 2 m.
Mark trip hazards on slab surface with high-visibility tape before inspector walkover begins.
Brief inspector on slab defects, uneven areas, and spalling locations visible from ground before scaffold access.
Conduct pre-inspection walk across scaffold platform to confirm stability, no movement, and no loose components.
Restrict inspection activity to daylight hours only — no night-time or poor-light assessment.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow inspector to access scaffold until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and received from licensed scaffolder
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start membrane application until: written inspection report and approval from Leo and Associates is received and slab repair scope is confirmed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold shows movement, loose components, or missing edge protection during pre-inspection walk
🛑 STOP WORK if: slab surface condition differs materially from pre-inspection briefing or reveals unknown structural defect
🛑 STOP WORK if: visibility or weather prevents safe slab assessment or inspector reports inability to complete inspection safely
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Provide Leo and Associates with current building plans, previous inspection records, and known defect locations.
tell building occupants of inspection date and scaffold presence; restrict occupant access to work area during inspection.
Record scaffold erection permit number, handover certificate date, and working at heights permit number on site documentation.
Retain written inspection report and Leo and Associates approval on file; do not proceed to membrane application without this approval.
Confirm Leo and Associates report includes crack mapping, spalling extent, moisture condition, and repair scope statement.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Hard hat (AS/NZS 1801 — helmet required for work at height)
eye protection— protection from dust and debris during visual inspection)
Steel-capped steel-capped footwear— grip and foot protection on uneven slab surface)
High-visibility vest (AS/NZS 1906.4 Class D — visibility on occupied site)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Before each day of inspection activity
monitoring.evidence: Handover certificate on file; visual confirmation of guardrail installation; working at heights permit posted on site

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion

tasks.task: Repair slab cracks and spalling per engineer scope
tasks.scope: Fill and repair slab cracks, spalling, and surface defects using approved repair materials and method as directed by Leo and Associates. Prepare surface to specification for waterproofing application. Allow cure time as required before proceeding
hazards: Inhalation of dust from grinding, cutting, and preparation of crack and spall edges
Chemical exposure from repair material mixing and application (epoxy, polyurethane, or cementitious systems)
Eye irritation or splash injury from liquid repair materials
Fall from height during repair work on balcony slab edges and perimeter
Musculoskeletal strain from repetitive grinding, filling, and finishing motions
Slip hazard from wet or sticky repair material residue on balcony surface
tasks.dominant_hazard: Chemical exposure or inhalation from repair material application
controls: Verify SDS for repair material on point of use before mixing or application starts.
Establish mechanical ventilation or natural cross-ventilation to disperse fumes during material application and cure.
Wet-grind or vacuum-grind crack and spall edges; prohibit dry grinding on occupied balcony slab.
Confirm substrate is clean, dry, and free of contaminants before repair material application — sign off on pre-application checklist.
Restrict occupant and pedestrian access to balcony during preparation, application, and initial cure using barricades and exclusion signage.
check repaired surface and confirm material has cured to engineer specification before waterproofing prep commences — hold point authority: Leo and Associates representative.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection
Clean tools and excess material immediately after application using approved solvent or water per SDS — do not allow material to set on balcony surface.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply waterproofing membrane until: Leo and Associates representative has inspected repaired slab surface, confirmed material cure is complete, and signed off pre-waterproofing checklist.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: SDS requirements cannot be met (ventilation fails, weather prevents outdoor cure, contamination occurs).
🛑 STOP WORK if: repair material contacts occupants or escapes exclusion zone during application or cure.
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate condition differs from engineer scope (unexpected structural defect, moisture ingress, or delamination discovered during preparation).
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and on site before any worker accesses balcony.
Obtain working at heights permit signed by authorised person before elevated repair work commences.
tell building management of occupancy restrictions and cure time windows at least 24 hours before work starts.
Record repair material lot numbers, application date, and cure completion on site log.
Retain SDS and material safety briefing sign-in sheet on site for EPA compliance.
ppe: Respirator or dust mask (type determined by repair material SDS and ventilation assessment)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during material application and initial cure; daily before occupants re-access balcony.
monitoring.evidence: SDS checklist signed before work; ventilation log or weather record; occupancy restriction signage photographed; material cure confirmation checklist.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Apply waterproofing membrane system to slab
tasks.scope: Apply new waterproofing membrane system to prepared slab according to product specification and Leo and Associates design. make sure continuous coverage, proper overlap, and sealing of all penetrations and edges. Allow cure time. Conduct membrane integrity testing if required
hazards: Chemical exposure or skin contact from membrane material (solvent-based, bitumen, or liquid polymer)
Inhalation of solvent fumes or volatile organic compounds during membrane application
Slip and fall hazard from wet or slippery membrane surface during application and cure
Fall from height while applying membrane to edges, penetrations, and perimeter zones
Flash fire or chemical reaction hazard if incompatible products mixed or applied in sequence
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of solvent fumes or volatile organic compounds
controls: Obtain and display current SDS for membrane product on site before application starts.
Verify substrate is clean, dry, and free from dust, loose material, and contaminants per product specification.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation across slab — air movement toward extraction or external wall, minimum velocity 0.5 m/s.
Prohibit smoking, naked flame, and hot work within 5 m of application and cure zones.
Confirm no incompatible products are stored or applied within 10 m of membrane zone — check application sequence with designer.
Apply membrane in thin, even coats following product-specified spread rate and overlap — measure overlap at 300 mm intervals with tape rule.
Barricade wet membrane zones with rope and signs — restrict access to authorised applicators only until surface is non-tacky.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves, hi-viz shirt or vest, and respiratory protective equipment (cartridge type P3) when airborne vapour is visible or detected.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: SDS is on site, substrate is inspected and signed off by supervisor, and weather/cure window is confirmed possible.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow foot traffic or load application until: full cure time per SDS is achieved and membrane integrity test is passed or waived in writing by designer.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: mechanical ventilation fails or wind direction reverses fumes toward occupied spaces.
🛑 STOP WORK if: incompatible product or sequence change is introduced without designer approval.
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate becomes wet, contaminated, or temperature/humidity falls outside product specification limits.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Verify all applicators hold current White Card and SDS training for membrane product.
tell building occupants of fume venting and access restrictions for cure period.
Record membrane batch number, application date, ambient conditions, and cure completion in site log.
Confirm designer approval before integrity testing method and acceptance criteria finalised.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: hi-viz shirt or vest, fluid-resistant preferred)
Respiratory protective equipment — cartridge type P3 (organic vapour + particulate) fitted to wearer
Non-slip footwear with grip sole (to reduce slip on damp surfaces)

monitoring.critical_control: Maintain continuous mechanical ventilation toward extraction during and 2 hours post-application.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during application; check every 30 minutes; verify post-application for 2 hours minimum
monitoring.evidence: Visual air movement confirmed (smoke tube or visual marker); ventilation fan running log; applicator sign-on sheet with time entries

responsibility.WKR: Perform Apply waterproofing membrane system to per SWMS

tasks.task: Install screed and waterproof all junctions
tasks.scope: Apply screed layer over membrane to achieve correct fall and levels. Seal all junctions with balustrades, edges, and penetrations. Allow full cure before tiling. Protect membrane during all subsequent works
hazards: Thermal or chemical burn from hot screed material or heated waterproofing compounds
Inhalation of dust or fumes during screed mixing and application
Fall from height during junction sealing work at balustrade, edge, and penetration points
Slip and fall hazard from wet screed or waterproofing sealant residue
Musculoskeletal strain from screed laying and finishing work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during junction sealing work at height
controls: Confirm scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses scaffold.
Obtain and display scaffold handover certificate at point of access before first worker ascends.
Check scaffold guard rails, mid-rails, and toe boards are intact and secure before screed work starts.
Establish wet suppression system: mist spray or damp sponges during screed mixing and application to control dust.
Apply SDS for waterproofing membrane and screed product on site before work starts.
Verify ventilation is adequate: extract fumes from heated compounds via openable windows or portable extraction at work level.
Barricade junction sealing points at balustrade and edge penetrations with temporary edge protection or barriers to prevent step-off during application.
Wear non-slip footwear with grip tread and check sole condition before each shift on wet screed surfaces.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start screed application until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and displayed, and weather conditions allow (calm, dry, within SDS cure temperature range)
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start junction sealing at height until: guard rails are in place, harness anchorage is tested and signed off, and SDS requirements are confirmed on site

🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 25 km/h or rain begins during sealant application
🛑 STOP WORK if: slip hazard from wet residue cannot be managed or harness cannot be secured to independent structure

task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during scaffold dismantling
controls: Dismantle scaffold in reverse erection sequence — follow original erection drawing and scaffolder's method statement exactly.
Install and maintain full edge protection and fall arrest points on all working platforms until final sections are removed.
Secure all tools and loose components with lanyards — no dropped object risk from height onto occupants below.
Barricade exclusion zone below scaffold during dismantling — prevent public and worker access; use spotters for all load movements.
Check scaffold structural integrity before each work shift — identify loose bolts, bent tubes, missing bracing, or instability.
Remove scaffold in small sections — do not overload platforms or create unsupported spans during partial dismantling.
Brief all workers on collapse risk and mandatory two-person minimum during dismantling — no solo work on scaffold.
Load scaffold components directly into vehicle or stack on ground under controlled movement — no throwing or dropping.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not dismantle first section until: original erection drawing reviewed, reverse sequence confirmed with licenced scaffolder, and all workers briefed on method.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove final edge protection or fall arrest points until: ground-level stacking and vehicle loading complete and site verified safe for occupants.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold section becomes unstable, loose, or shows signs of collapse during dismantling.
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by occupants, vehicles, or unauthorised personnel during active dismantling.
🛑 STOP WORK if: fall arrest equipment, harnesses, or edge protection becomes damaged or non-compliant — do not continue elevated work.
admin: Confirm licenced scaffolder present and supervising dismantling — compliance with WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.6.
Verify working at heights permit signed and current before dismantling commences.
Obtain and retain scaffold handover certificate confirming structural condition pre-dismantling.
Issue site induction and occupancy briefing to all workers — residential occupants must understand exclusion zone and dust suppression.
Record all scaffold defects, damage, or non-standard conditions discovered during dismantling in site log.
Coordinate with occupants — tell timing of dismantling, noise, dust, and access restrictions.
Comply with EPA licence conditions — noise, dust, waste management during demobilisation.
Restore all access routes and courtyard to pre-works condition — photograph final state for handover.
ppe: Safety harness and lanyard (certified, load-rated minimum 15 kN) — mandatory for all elevated work
Dust mask (P2 minimum) — if dust generated during dismantling

monitoring.critical_control: Check scaffold bolts, bracing, and platform stability before each 2-hour work shift — report any looseness or misalignment immediately.
monitoring.frequency: before work start each shift, after any significant wind event, continuously during dismantling
monitoring.evidence: Site supervisor checklist signed; photo log of each removed section; defect register entry if issues found

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues
